risks: The study adds no intervention; risks are to privacy and the burden of a few extra minutes per call. Tapering itself carries withdrawal and overdose risk, managed by the pathway's naloxone supply and same-week review, not by the study.
consent: Written consent at entry to the pathway for research use of pathway data, dispensing history and hospital attendances for 12 months, including after leaving the pathway. Declining has no effect on care. Consent is taken with a professional interpreter when needed.
data: Coded data on the hospital's research drive; the key is held by the pharmacist; dispensing and hospital data are extracted for consenting participants only.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: place of residence (patients up to 150 km away), language (interpreter need), disability and mental health (depression screen) and socioeconomic position. Interpreter-supported calls are offered and outcomes are reported separately for distant patients and those needing an interpreter.
effectiveness: The study informs, but cannot prove, the pathway's effect; its value is honest outcome data for the 2027 decision.
efficiency: Uses existing calls and 0.4 FTE; no new clinic visits.
costs: Interpreter time for consent and calls; no other new costs.
grants: None needed; a hospital small grant could fund interpreter time.
partnerships: Clinic physicians, community pharmacies that dispense tapered doses, and two patient partners who have tapered with the pathway.
rebPath: Hospital research ethics board review under ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki; submission planned for 2026-10-20 and no research data collected before approval.
limitations: Single clinic, no comparison group, self-selected participants.
summary: Low-risk observational study with consent that covers follow-up after leaving, interpreter support and an equity split by distance and language.
